# Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 22 (Bu-Vb Pc22)

**ID:** Bu-Vb Pc22  
**Section:** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga (bu-vb)

**Title (English, from literature):** Instructing nuns after sunset

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 22, titled *Atthaṅgata* ("Instructing nuns after sunset" in Bhikkhu Brahmali's translation), establishes that a Buddhist monk who continues or undertakes the instruction of nuns after the sun has set commits an offense that must be confessed (*pācittiya*).

Full parallels to this rule exist across virtually all known Vinaya traditions, preserved in the Pali Bhikkhu Pātimokkha (*pli-tv-bu-pm-pc22*) and Bhikkhu Parivāra, as well as the Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Mahīśāsaka, Mahāsaṅghika, Dharmaguptaka, Kāśyapīya, and Upāliparipṛcchā lineages in Chinese, Sanskrit, and Tibetan translations. Further passage-level parallels are identified in Udāna 4.7 (PTS Ud 43), Theragāthā 1.68, several versions of the Udānavarga, and fragmentary Sanskrit Bhikkhu Pātimokkha texts from Turfan and Gilgit.

None of the secondary literature excerpts supplied in the dossier concern this rule; they refer instead to Jain historical texts, Nissaggiya Pācittiya 22, or Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 22.

*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on catalog data.*
